'''Karma Dajani''' is a Lebanese-Dutch mathematician whose research interests include [[ergodic theory]], [[probability theory]], and their applications in [[number theory]].{{r|egmo}} She is an associate professor of mathematics at [[Utrecht University]].{{r|profile}}

==Education and career==
Dajani was born in Lebanon,{{r|egmo2}} and did her undergraduate studies at the [[American University of Beirut]],{{r|aub}} initially in medicine but switching after a year to mathematics.{{r|egmo2}}

Because of the [[Lebanese Civil War]], she and her family moved to the US,{{r|egmo2}}
where she earned her Ph.D. in 1989 from [[George Washington University]].{{r|mg}} Again, she switched topics, beginning in [[functional analysis]] and trying [[graph theory]] but ending in [[ergodic theory]].{{r|egmo2}} Her dissertation, ''Simultaneous Recurrence of Weighted Cocycles'', was supervised by E. Arthur Robinson Jr.,{{r|mg}} after a previous advisor, Daniel Ullman, shifted his own interests away from ergodic theory.{{r|egmo2}} As a student at George Washington University, Dajani was a two-time winner of the university's Taylor Prize in Mathematics.{{r|taylor}}

After completing her doctorate, she was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] and the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]].{{r|egmo2}} She took a faculty position at the [[University of Alabama]]{{r|egmo2|aub}}. 
After marrying a Dutch mathematician, Cor Kraaikamp, she obtained a visiting position at [[Delft University of Technology]] and then joined Utrecht University.{{r|egmo2}} She spent 25 years as the only female mathematics professor at Utrecht.{{r|egmo}}

==Book==
With her husband Cor Kraaikamp, Dajani is the author of the book ''Ergodic Theory of Numbers'', published in 2002 by the [[Mathematical Association of America]] as volume 29 of their [[Carus Mathematical Monographs]].{{r|etn}} The book grew out of a course given by Dajani in a 1996 summer program for women in mathematics.{{sfnp|Ward|2003}}
